docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
Games programmer with Unreal Engine, Unity, and backend engineering experience.

Like many in this field, I grew up as a gamer. I spent too many hours playing and wondering what it would be like to see my name in the credits one day. That dream stuck with me - and eventually, it came true.

I dedicated both my undergraduate and postgraduate studies to games technology, and since then, I have worked on a range of projects using Unreal Engine, Unity, and backend systems. I genuinely enjoy digging into complex systems, solving tricky problems, and figuring out how everything works under the hood.

I do not claim to be the fastest learner in the room, but I have always believed that consistency beats speed. I keep showing up, keep learning, and keep building - and that has made all the difference in my journey so far.

docs.title: Down Current
docs.text:
A 3D narrative game developed in Unreal Engine 4.

Download Here

June 2022 - August 2022

Down Current is a 3D narrative game created as part of the final assessment of the MProf in Games Development at Abertay University.

It was developed within 12 weeks using Unreal Engine 4, under mentorship from The Chinese Room.

I was the lead programmer in a team of nine Master's students. My work included implementing player logic, a custom spell system, UI implementation, and related gameplay systems.

docs.title: Player Climbing
docs.text: I implemented climbing mechanics for a flexible first-person climbing experience, expanding player movement vertically. The system lets the player move horizontally and vertically, rotate the camera while climbing, and automatically climb up when reaching the top of a surface.

docs.title: Spell Casting System
docs.text: This is the player's primary mechanic. By inputting the correct button sequence, the player can direct Genhu to purify toxic sludge areas and assist exploration. I implemented the system structure and the player input side, leaving Genhu's specific behavior decoupled for another programmer.

docs.title: Input Device Update
docs.text: Down Current was designed for both PC and console. Players can use keyboard and mouse or a controller. I created an event listener for input device updates so UI icons and text could change when a new controller is connected during play.

docs.title: Interaction System
docs.text: Implemented the interaction system, allowing the player to interact with objects in the scene and unlock corresponding entries in the journal.

docs.title: Linear Dialogue System
docs.text: Implemented short dialogue lines that appear when the player interacts with the Parched NPCs. Each Parched character has different moods and triggers different dialogue categories depending on their mood.

docs.title: Level Streaming
docs.text: Implemented level streaming to load and unload maps asynchronously during splash and loading screens.

docs.title: Florere Memoriae
docs.text:
A Victorian flower-language game developed in Unreal Engine 4.

Download Here

March 2022 - June 2022

Inspired by the Victorian era, Florere Memoriae creates a journey of nostalgia and love using Victorian flower language in a forest painted before the player's eyes. With each discovery, the forest reveals more of its colors, and each relieved memory makes new flowers bloom in the world.

It was developed within ten weeks using Unreal Engine 4. I was the only programmer in a team of six students and oversaw the implementation of all gameplay mechanics.

docs.title: Interactable Items
docs.text: There are two types of interactable items in the game: objects that the player collects during the game and flowers. I implemented the base class structure that other interactable items derive from.

docs.title: Logbook System
docs.text: The logbook gives players more information about flowers collected during the game. I designed a data structure for plant data so each logbook slot could store the needed images, names, descriptions, and categories.

docs.title: Visual Effects
docs.text: Implemented a dynamic material transition effect to make state changes feel more natural. The effect uses pixel depth to calculate the distance between rendered mesh pixels and the camera, allowing generation speed to vary by distance.

docs.title: Hunt: Showdown
docs.text:
Backend programming for a large-scale multiplayer project.

September 2023 - May 2024

Fully embedded in Crytek's backend team via Stainless Games, participating in daily standups, sprint planning, and code reviews alongside internal staff.

  • Contributed directly to delivering a high-performance backend for large-scale multiplayer.
  • Developed API testing and internal validation tools using Go, improving system stability and efficiency.
  • Contributed to debugging and refining architecture for improved scalability and performance.
  • Adapted quickly to Crytek's workflows and proprietary infrastructure, integrating into their engineering processes.

docs.title: Wickie: Defender of Kitties
docs.text:
A 3D strategy game developed in Unity.

View Source Code

September 2021 - December 2021

Wickie: Defender of Kitties is a 3D strategy game created by a team of five students from Abertay University. It was developed within 12 weeks using Unity.

docs.title: Lighthouse Abilities
docs.text: Implemented a component-based expandable ability system. As the core mechanic, the player controls a lighthouse to protect ships from monsters. The player can use resources collected during the game to upgrade lighthouse abilities.

docs.title: World Bending Shader
docs.text: Implemented an Animal Crossing style world bending shader, added in response to project feedback.

docs.title: Level Configs
docs.text: Used ScriptableObject as a container to store level configuration data for each level.
